newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aberfoyle buy boosts ConsGold output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aberfoyle buy boosts ConsGold output.

text.p: Consolidated Gold NL said on Thursday its purchase of Aberfoyle Ltd's gold assets at Davyhurst in the Riverina region would push ConsGold's annual production to about 160,000 ounces.

"ConsGold will purchase Aberfoyle's Lights of Israel underground gold mine near Davyhurst, which commenced production in September 1996 and the Bardoc treatment plant, which will be moved to Davyhurst and upgraded to one million tonnes per annum," ConsGold said.

Earlier it was announced that ConsGold would issue 38 million or 19.5 percent of its shares to Aberfoyle at 40 cents per share and would have a one-for-two renounceable rights issue to shareholders at 35 cents each to raise A$18.2 million.
The rights issue is being underwritten by J.B. Were with Porter Western Ltd as sponsoring broker and underwriter.
"The funds have been earmarked for the relocation and upgrading of the Bardoc treatment plant and acceleration of the current exploration programme at Kookynie," ConsGold said.
It had received indicative funding offers from several banks for up to A$10 million to support the construction programme at Kooknyie.
Approval for the issues would be sought from shareholders at the November 1 annual meeting.
"ConsGold has just stepped into a new league," ConsGold executive chairman George Jones said in a statement.

"The company will be the dominant and most strategically placed (company) in two highly prospective goldfields regions, produce approximately 160,000 ounces of gold a year, and have the ground position, size and financial muscle to continue to push towards our goal of becoming a major Western Australin gold group," ConsGold said.
ConsGold's share price closed up one cent at 46 cents while Aberfoyle's shares closed up two cents at A$2.99.
